bib.title: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers

question: Can self-attention keep content-based (learned) sparsity while using natively sparse attention matrices, so cost drops below quadratic in sequence length?
hypothesis: Routing queries to keys in the same online spherical k-means cluster approximates maximum inner product search, keeps large attention weights, and beats fixed local/strided sparsity patterns.
contributions: Routing attention: online k-means clustering of queries and keys, attention only within a cluster, O(n^1.5 d) cost
State of the art on Wikitext-103, PG-19 and ImageNet-64, competitive on enwik-8
Evidence that scaled-up local attention is a strong baseline
Ablations on CIFAR-10 and a Jensen-Shannon analysis of routing versus local heads

method.summary: Each attention layer clusters queries and keys with shared centroids learned by exponential moving average; each centroid keeps the top n/k tokens by distance, and attention is dense within each cluster. Routing heads are mixed with local-attention heads; keys and queries are shared in causal models.
method.task: autoregressive language modeling and image generation

datasets.name: Wikitext-103
datasets.size: over 100 million tokens from 28K articles, avg 3.6K tokens per article

datasets.name: ImageNet 64x64
datasets.size: images of 64x64x3 bytes as sequences of length 12,288, raster RGB order

datasets.name: PG-19
datasets.size: approximately 28,000 books, 1.9 billion tokens, avg context roughly 69,000 words
datasets.split: test perplexity normalized by token counts of Rae et al. 2020

models.name: Routing Transformer (PG-19)
models.architecture: 2 routing heads, routing only in last two layers

models.name: Local Transformer, Transformer-XL, Sparse Transformer, Compressive Transformer, Adaptive models, Reformer

training.optimizer: Adam (beta1 0.9, beta2 0.98) for all but PG-19; Adafactor for PG-19
training.lr_schedule: schedule of Vaswani et al. 2017 (Adam); PG-19 linear warmup then rsqrt_normalized_decay
training.seq_len: 3072 CIFAR-10; 8192 enwik-8 and PG-19; 12,288 ImageNet-64; 4096 for the JSD analysis on Wikitext-103

other.centroid update: EMA, decay lambda usually 0.999; padding tokens excluded
other.head allocation: half local, half routing in all models except PG-19
other.PG-19 deviations: 2 routing heads, routing in last two layers only, Adafactor

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: test-set, PG-19 normalized by token counts of Rae et al. 2020

metrics.name: step time
metrics.definition: training steps per second on TPUv3, same cores and batch size

metrics.name: Jensen-Shannon divergence
metrics.definition: between attention distributions of local and routing heads, natural log, max 0.6931

eval.protocol: Single reported runs; no seeds or significance test stated except JSD over 10 runs.

limits: Wall-clock is slower than local attention on TPU (no sparse ops); authors say wall-clock is only a secondary goal
Top-k balanced assignment does not guarantee each point belongs to a single cluster
Full attention only compared on the short CIFAR-10 sequences; best routing models beat full attention but not by enough to rule out noise
Sparse attention trains on long sequences so fits fewer layers than Transformer-XL style recurrence
No seeds or variance for main results; compute not stated
Training-time method for autoregressive models; no KV-cache or decode-time latency measurement
Dated: later long-context methods (e.g. FlashAttention-style dense kernels) changed the speed trade-off
